newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-FERGUS LEADS LAS VEGAS INVITATIONAL AFTER SHOOTING 62.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-FERGUS LEADS LAS VEGAS INVITATIONAL AFTER SHOOTING 62.

text.p: Keith Fergus, who left the PGA Tour for nearly seven years to become the golf coach at the University of Houston, fired a sizzling 10-under-par 62 on Wednesday to take the lead after the first round of the Las Vegas Invitational.
Fergus recorded nine birdies, an eagle and just one bogey for his round, which tied the record for the TPC at Summerlin course, one of three being used in the 90-hole tournament.
His 62 gave him just a one-stroke cushion, however, over Fred Funk and Payne Stewart.
Stewart notched his 63 on the Summerlin layout, while Funk played the par-71 Las Vegas Hilton course. The other course in the rotation is the par-72 Desert Inn Golf Club layout.
Mike Sullivan, Rick Fehr, Wayne Levi and Ronnie Black were two shots back at 64, while David Frost of South Africa was another stroke behind at 65.
Fergus said when he made the turn at 6-under 30, he began thinking of tying the PGA Tour single-round record of 59.
"After the front nine, I got to thinking I might shoot 59," Fergus said. "It crossed my mind, but then I three-putted 11 and I quickly forgot about that."
Funk, currently the hottest player on Tour, created a bit of controversy when he criticised media coverage of heralded young professional Tiger Woods.
Woods was quoted as saying in local newspapers he was disappointed not to get to play the final round of the B.C. Open, which was washed out by rain, because he felt he was in a position to win.
Funk, who won that rain-shortened event, took exception to Woods' remarks, which he said fired him up for the day.
The article made it seem like it was all Tiger and I was out there with a 6-shot lead," Funk complained. "That got me fired up. I was ready to go after I read that."
Woods shot a one-under 70 on the same Las Vegas Hilton layout that Funk carded his 63 Wednesday.
